name: Prado Museum
places: Goya Monument, beside the Prado Museum
description: Spain’s national art museum, built on the royal collections: Velázquez, Goya, El Greco and Bosch. A statue of Goya stands outside.

name: Puerta del Sol
description: Madrid’s busiest square. A plaque on the pavement marks kilometre zero of Spain’s roads, and crowds gather under the clock on New Year’s Eve.

name: Plaza Mayor
description: A big arcaded 17th-century square in the old town, once used for markets, bullfights and public executions.

name: Las Ventas bullring
description: Madrid’s bullring, a large brick and tile building from the 1930s in neo-Mudéjar style. It also hosts concerts.

name: Congress of Deputies
description: The lower house of Spain’s parliament, in a 19th-century building guarded by two bronze lions.

name: Santiago Bernabéu Stadium
description: Real Madrid’s home stadium on the Paseo de la Castellana, with a club museum and stadium tour.

name: Atocha station
description: Madrid’s main railway station, built around a 19th-century iron and glass train hall.

name: Valley of the Fallen
description: A basilica cut into a mountain outside Madrid under a huge stone cross, built by Franco’s regime partly with prisoners’ labour.

name: Reina Sofía Museum
description: Spain’s national museum of modern and contemporary art, in a former hospital. Picasso’s Guernica hangs here.

name: Royal Palace of Aranjuez
description: A royal palace with large gardens in the town of Aranjuez, south of Madrid, long used by Spanish kings as a spring residence.

name: Plaza de Santa Ana
places: Lorca statue, Plaza de Santa Ana
description: A lively square in the old literary quarter, lined with bars and the Teatro Español, with a statue of the poet Lorca.

name: El Escorial
places: Friars’ Garden, Royal Monastery of El Escorial
description: A vast 16th-century monastery and royal palace in the hills northwest of Madrid, with a basilica, library, royal tombs and terraced gardens.
